parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of gender expression or same-sex conduct, no documented universal facility, border or care exclusion, and visible LGBT scene/Pride mitigate risk. However, documented police targeting, extortion/abuse and forced humiliating bathing of transgender women—especially sex workers—in one city, plus >135 harassment/abuse cases and a 2016 survey finding 38% of surveyed trans women arrested mostly because they were trans, show state-tolerated targeting. No operative anti-discrimination protection or documented remedy offsets this; UPR acceptances are unenacted. Custody protection is only an undocumented, surgery-gated remark. Street/police exposure for an outed visitor is therefore substantial, without reaching systematic imprisonment or universal exclusion.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police targeting of transgender women, including extortion/abuse and forced bathing/leaving area in one city; 38% of surveyed trans women reported arrest mostly because trans.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2025 remark says post-surgery trans prisoners transferred from men's to women's facility at one prison; not a published regulation.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Surgery is not legally available and no placement is documented for non-surgery prisoners, so the remark gives no reliable visitor protection if detained.

care_services.protection: Foreign-government report found no official discrimination based on sexual orientation in health care; no trans-specific visitor care evidence documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans-specific criminal offence, but police harassment/abuse and arrests linked to being trans are documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Government rhetoric and tourism welcome campaign, but no enacted anti-discrimination protection; official claims of protection disputed.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Cooperative paper posture does not change documented street-level police practice.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: >135 harassment/abuse cases against transgender women on city streets; >100 violence/abuse incidents reported in 2017; violence listed among significant human-rights issues.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Counts are monitoring figures, not rates, but pattern plus police involvement raises exposure beyond isolated incidents.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No operative legal protection or documented remedy for discrimination/harassment; resident legal recognition absent, though not itself a visitor exposure.
remedies_unknowns.protection: UN expert visit and UPR acceptances show engagement but are not enacted protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unenacted acceptances and disputed official claims cannot offset documented enforcement practice.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar police extortion/abuse of visibly trans people, but here targeting is documented mainly for transgender sex workers in one city and street harassment, not routine stops of foreign travellers in terminals/markets; hence higher than 0.35.

Similar in having recurring visitor-facing harassment with incomplete remedies and no universal rule, but here there is no documented successful remedy—no readmissions, compensation or prosecutions—so lower than 0.55.

Higher than 0.75 because that anchor has established gender-diverse respect, dead-letter sexuality law, enforced court compensation and identity-based facilities; here police targeting and unremedied street abuse are documented and protections are not operative.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: no criminal or universal institutional exclusion, but outed visibility can lead to police abuse/extortion and street harassment, especially in the identified city and sex-work contexts. Tourism welcome, Pride visibility and cooperative international posture are real but non-operative signals. Absent documented prosecution, compensation, facility or custody guarantees, recourse is thin. This places the jurisdiction in Elevated Risk, below partial-remedy cases and above systematic detention/universal-exclusion cases.
